import hashlib,json
far=next(o for o in raw['objects'] if o['name']=='M4_Far_00'); near=next(o for o in raw['objects'] if o['name']=='M4_Near')
for obj in [far,near]:
 vertices=np.asarray(obj['vertices']); triangles=np.asarray(obj['triangles']); normals=np.cross(vertices[triangles[:,1]]-vertices[triangles[:,0]],vertices[triangles[:,2]]-vertices[triangles[:,0]]); normals/=np.linalg.norm(normals,axis=1)[:,None]
 print(obj['name'],'count',len(triangles),'bounds',vertices.min(0).tolist(),vertices.max(0).tolist(),'normals',np.unique(normals,axis=0).tolist())
 print('ordered_geometry_sha256_json',hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({'vertices':obj['vertices'],'triangles':obj['triangles']},separators=(',',':')).encode()).hexdigest())
 if obj is far:
  for first,last in [(0,511),(512,513)]:
   patch=vertices[triangles[first:last+1]]; print('region',first,last,'bounds',patch.min((0,1)).tolist(),patch.max((0,1)).tolist(),'normal',normals[first].tolist())
# Global lower bound: every far point has x>=1, every near point has x=near_x.
# Vertex pair attains this bound; all source triangles included in bounds.
a=np.asarray(far['vertices'][0]); b=np.asarray(near['vertices'][0]); delta=b-a
